_meta.ci_method: paired percentile bootstrap; the resampling unit is stated per row. ImageNet-C previously resampled 135 correlated cell-seed rows i.i.d. while the manuscript described a seed-averaged condition-level design; the condition-level design is the one reported. CIFAR-10-C rows additionally report cluster-robust intervals at 216 twin-pairs, 12 corruption x severity clusters and 6 corruption families, because the 432 grid cells are not 432 independent draws (r0/r1 replicate correlation 0.948-0.999).
_meta.rule: BEATS-BOTH = regret_kga < adapt AND < freeze AND the 95% CI on the gap to the BETTER policy excludes 0 AND clean held-out. CLUSTER-ROBUST BEATS-BOTH additionally requires the interval to exclude 0 when whole corruption families are the resampling unit. NO-HARM = ties better + beats worse + FA_u <= alpha; FAIL = FA_u > alpha; else NULL.
_meta.integrity: scored once; every arm reported; Camelyon-G withdrawn not reinstated; frozen bars consumed for locked datasets (no re-roll); only ImageNet-C newly scored
_meta.wave_holm_family: SUPERSEDED. The previous value -- '3 beats-both candidates (CIFAR-10-C tent/eata vs adapt; ImageNet-C sar vs freeze); all survive Holm at 0.05' -- named exactly the three comparisons that came out positive, after the results were known. That is not a multiplicity family and it is withdrawn. The confirmatory family is now declared PROSPECTIVELY as the set of pre-registered beats-both bars: one per (track, candidate) pair named in a research_lock/ protocol file BEFORE any number for that pair was computed, each evaluated once on its declared test cells. Rows from development screens, superseded protocol versions or post hoc re-scorings are not members and are not eligible for promotion. Holm is applied over that inventory, published in full (including failures) as Appendix 'Pre-registered arm inventory' / tab:arm-inventory. Denominator for context: 1387 recorded beats_both determinations project-wide (326 true, 23.5% base rate) over 70 scored result units and 69 protocol files.
